title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 87 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 484–486 (Night 87, continuing directly from nights-86), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 87 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. Ḍawʾ al-Makān distributes the Damascus tribute to the army, returns to Baghdad and takes the throne, and sends the vizier Dandān to his brother Sharrukān with a letter calling him to the war against the unbelievers. Sharrukān arrives with the armies of Syria, the brothers meet and weep, and a month is spent gathering the host, until dawn cuts Shahrazād off. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ السَّابِعَةُ وَالثَّمَانُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-sābiʿatu wa-al-thamānūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the seventh and the eighty,
sentences.i: And when it was the eighty-seventh night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدَأَنَّ ضَوْءَالْمَكَانِ أَمَرَ الْحَاجِبَ أَنْ يَعْرِضَ عَلَيْهِ مَا أَتَى بِهِ مِنْ خَرَاجِ دِمَشْقَ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīda anna ḍawʾa al-makāni amara al-ḥājiba an yaʿriḍa ʿalayhi mā atā bihi min kharāji dimashqa
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that Ḍawʾ al-Makān commanded the chamberlain to present to him what he had brought of the tribute of Damascus,
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that Ḍawʾ al-Makān commanded the chamberlain to lay before him what he had brought in tribute from Damascus.
sentences.n: The print runs أن (“that”) into the word before it (السعيدأن, “the happy — that”) and sets ضوءالمكان as one word; both are read as two words, and the spacing is kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَعَرَضَ عَلَيْهِ صَنَادِيقَ الْمَالِ وَالتُّحَفِ وَالْجَوَاهِرِ فَأَخَذَهَا وَفَرَّقَهَا عَلَى الْعَسَاكِرِ وَلَمْ يُبْقِ مِنْهَا شَيْأً أَبَدًا
sentences.tr: fa-ʿaraḍa ʿalayhi ṣanādīqa al-māli wa-al-tuḥafi wa-al-jawāhiri fa-akhadhahā wa-farraqahā ʿalā al-ʿasākiri wa-lam yubqi minhā shayʾan abadan
sentences.l: So he presented to him the chests of the money and the rarities and the jewels, and he took them and distributed them upon the armies, and did not leave of them a thing, ever.
sentences.i: So the chamberlain laid before him the chests of money, the rarities and the jewels, and he took them and shared them out among the troops, leaving nothing of them at all.

sentences.t: فَقَبَّلَ الْأُمَرَاءُ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَدَعَوْا لَهُ بِطُولِ الْبَقَاءِ وَقَالُوا مَا رَأَيْنَا مَلِكًا يُعْطِي مِثْلَ هَذِهِ الْعَطَايَا
sentences.tr: fa-qabbala al-umarāʾu al-arḍa bayna yadayhi wa-daʿaw lahu bi-ṭūli al-baqāʾi wa-qālū mā raʾaynā malikan yuʿṭī mithla hādhihi al-ʿaṭāyā
sentences.l: And the emirs kissed the ground between his hands, and prayed for him with length of abiding, and said: We have not seen a king who gives the like of these gifts.
sentences.i: The emirs kissed the ground before him and prayed that he might live long, and they said: “We have never seen a king who gives such gifts.”
sentences.n: “Kissed the ground between his hands” is the stock courtly gesture of homage.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ مَضَوْا إِلَى خِيَامِهِمْ فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحُوا أَمَرَهُمْ بِالسَّفَرِ فَسَافَرُوا ثَلْثَةَ أَيَّامٍ وَفِى الْيَوْمِ الرَّابِعِ أَشْرَفُوا عَلَى بَغْدَادَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahum maḍaw ilā khiyāmihim fa-lammā aṣbaḥū amarahum bi-al-safari fa-sāfarū thalthata ayyāmin wa-fī al-yawmi al-rābiʿi ashrafū ʿalā baghdāda
sentences.l: Then they went to their tents, and when they reached the morning he commanded them to the journey, and they journeyed three days, and in the day the fourth they overlooked Baghdad.
sentences.i: Then they went off to their tents, and when morning came he ordered them to set out, and they travelled for three days, and on the fourth day they came in sight of Baghdad.
sentences.n: ثلثة is the edition’s spelling of ثلاثة “three”, and فى of في “in”; both are kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلُوا الْمَدِينَةَ فَوَجَدُوهَا قَدْ تَزَيَّنَتْ وَطَلَعَ السُّلْطَانُ ضَوْءُالْمَكَانِ قَصْرَ أَبِيهِ وَجَلَسَ عَلَى السَّرِيرِ وَوَقَفَ أُمَرَاءُ الْعَسْكَرِ وَالْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ وَحَاجِبُ دِمَشْقَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhalū al-madīnata fa-wajadūhā qad tazayyanat wa-ṭalaʿa al-sulṭānu ḍawʾu al-makāni qaṣra abīhi wa-jalasa ʿalā al-sarīri wa-waqafa umarāʾu al-ʿaskari wa-al-wazīru dandānu wa-ḥājibu dimashqa bayna yadayhi
sentences.l: So they entered the city and found it had adorned itself, and the sultan Ḍawʾ al-Makān went up to the palace of his father, and sat upon the throne, and the emirs of the army stood, and the vizier Dandān, and the chamberlain of Damascus, between his hands.
sentences.i: They entered the city and found it decked out in their honour, and the sultan Ḍawʾ al-Makān went up into his father’s palace and sat on the throne, while the emirs of the army, the vizier Dandān and the chamberlain of Damascus stood before him.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ أَمَرَ كَاتِبَ السِّرِّأَنْ يَكْتُبَ كِتَابًا إِلَى أَخِيهِ شَرْكَانَ وَيَذْكُرَ فِيهِ مَا جَرَى مِنَ الْأَوَّلِ إِلَى الْآخِرِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika amara kātiba al-sirri an yaktuba kitāban ilā akhīhi sharrukāna wa-yadhkura fīhi mā jarā min al-awwali ilā al-ākhiri
sentences.l: So at that he commanded the writer of the secret to write a letter to his brother Sharrukān, and to mention in it what had happened from the first to the last,
sentences.i: At that he ordered his private secretary to write a letter to his brother Sharrukān, telling in it all that had happened from beginning to end,
sentences.n: The print has السّران, with a shadda on the sīn and the following أن run on to it; it is read as السر أن, “the secret — that”, and the spacing is kept as printed. كاتب السر, “writer of the secret”, is the secretary who keeps the ruler’s private correspondence.

sentences.t: وَيَذْكُرَ فِي آخِرِهِ وَسَاعَةَ وُقُوفِكَ عَلَى هَذَا الْمَكْتُوبِ تُجَهِّزْ أَمْرَكَ وَتَحْضُرْ بِعَسْكَرِكَ حَتَّى نَتَوَجَّهَ إِلَى غَزْوِ الْكُفَّارِ وَنَأْخُذَ لِوَالِدِنَا مِنْهُمُ الثَّأْرَ وَنَكْشِفَ عَنَّا الْعَارَ
sentences.tr: wa-yadhkura fī ākhirihi wa-sāʿata wuqūfika ʿalā hādhā al-maktūbi tujahhiz amraka wa-taḥḍur bi-ʿaskarika ḥattā natawajjaha ilā ghazwi al-kuffāri wa-naʾkhudha li-wālidinā minhumu al-thaʾra wa-nakshifa ʿannā al-ʿāra
sentences.l: and to mention at its end: And the hour of your standing upon this writing, prepare your affair and present yourself with your army, until we set out to the raiding of the unbelievers, and take for our father from them the blood-revenge, and uncover from us the shame.
sentences.i: and to say at the end: “The moment you read this letter, make ready and come with your army, so that we may march on the unbelievers, take vengeance on them for our father and wipe away our shame.”
sentences.n: The print has اى for إلى, a misprint for الى, corrected here. تجهز and تحضر follow the print’s bare forms and are read as commands (“you are to prepare … and come”), as the sense requires.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ طَوَى الْكِتَابَ وَخَتَمَهُ وَقَالَ لِلْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ مَا يَتَوَجَّهُ بِهَذَا الْكِتَابِ إِلَّا أَنْتَ وَلَكِنْ يَنْبَغِي أَنْ تَتَلَطَّفَ بِهِ فِى الْكَلَامِ
sentences.tr: thumma ṭawā al-kitāba wa-khatamahu wa-qāla li-al-wazīri dandāna mā yatawajjahu bi-hādhā al-kitābi illā anta wa-lākin yanbaghī an tatalaṭṭafa bihi fī al-kalāmi
sentences.l: Then he folded the book and sealed it, and said to the vizier Dandān: None goes with this book except you, but it is fitting that you be gentle with it in the speech,
sentences.i: Then he folded the letter and sealed it, and said to the vizier Dandān: “No one can take this letter but you, and you must be gentle in how you put it,
sentences.n: bi-hi here points back to the matter of the letter: “be gentle with it”, that is, in presenting it. فى is the print’s spelling of في.

sentences.t: وَتَقُولَ لَهُ إِنْ أَرَدْتَ مُلْكَ أَبِيكَ فَهُوَ لَكَ وَأَخُوكَ يَكُونُ نَائِبًا عَنْكَ فِي دِمَشْقَ كَمَا أَخْبَرَنَا بِذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-taqūla lahu in aradta mulka abīka fa-huwa laka wa-akhūka yakūnu nāʾiban ʿanka fī dimashqa kamā akhbaranā bi-dhālika
sentences.l: and that you say to him: If you wanted the kingdom of your father, it is yours, and your brother will be a deputy for you in Damascus, as he informed us of that.
sentences.i: and tell him: ‘If you want your father’s kingdom, it is yours, and I will be your deputy in Damascus, as he told us he would.’”
sentences.n: The Arabic has “your brother will be a deputy”, the speaker naming himself in the third person; the idiomatic layer says “I”.

sentences.t: فَنَزَلَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ مِنْ عِنْدِهِ وَتَجَهَّزَ لِلسَّفَرِ
sentences.tr: fa-nazala al-wazīru dandānu min ʿindihi wa-tajahhaza li-al-safari
sentences.l: So the vizier Dandān went down from him and made himself ready for the journey.
sentences.i: So the vizier Dandān left him and made ready for the journey.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ أَمَرَ أَنْ يَجْعَلُوا لِلْوَقَّادِ مَكَانًا فَاخِرًا وَيَفْرُشُوهُ بِأَحْسَنِ الْفَرْشِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna ḍawʾa al-makāni amara an yajʿalū li-al-waqqādi makānan fākhiran wa-yafrushūhu bi-aḥsani al-farshi
sentences.l: Then Ḍawʾ al-Makān commanded that they make for the fire-tender a splendid place, and furnish it with the finest of furnishings.
sentences.i: Then Ḍawʾ al-Makān gave orders that a splendid place be made ready for the fire-tender and furnished with the finest furnishings.
sentences.n: يجعلوا and يفرشوه lack the final nūn that the subjunctive after أن would keep in Classical Arabic (يجعلوا, يفرشوا); the print’s forms are read as they stand. The Waqqād (“fire-tender”) is the man who sheltered Ḍawʾ al-Makān in the earlier part of the tale.

sentences.t: وَذَلِكَ الْوَقَّادُ لَهُ حَدِيثٌ طَوِيلٌ
sentences.tr: wa-dhālika al-waqqādu lahu ḥadīthun ṭawīlun
sentences.l: And that fire-tender, to him is a long story.
sentences.i: And that fire-tender has a long story of his own.
sentences.n: The narrator’s aside points ahead to the part the fire-tender will play later in the tale.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ خَرَجَ يَوْمًا إِلَى الصَّيْدِ وَالْقَنْصِ وَعَادَ إِلَى بَغْدَادَ
sentences.tr: thumma inna ḍawʾa al-makāni kharaja yawman ilā al-ṣaydi wa-al-qanṣi wa-ʿāda ilā baghdāda
sentences.l: Then Ḍawʾ al-Makān went out one day to the hunting and the sport, and returned to Baghdad.
sentences.i: One day Ḍawʾ al-Makān went out hunting and coursing, and returned to Baghdad.
sentences.n: The print has اى for إلى, a misprint for الى, corrected here.

sentences.t: فَقَدَّمَ لَهُ بَعْضُ الْأُمَرَاءِ مِنَ الْخُيُولِ الْجِيَادِ وَمِنَ الْجَوَارِى الْحِسَانِ مَا يَعْجِزُ عَنْ وَصْفِهِ اللِّسَانُ
sentences.tr: fa-qaddama lahu baʿḍu al-umarāʾi mina al-khuyūli al-jiyādi wa-mina al-jawārī al-ḥisāni mā yaʿjizu ʿan waṣfihi al-lisānu
sentences.l: And one of the emirs presented to him, of the swift horses and of the beautiful slave-girls, what the tongue is unable to describe.
sentences.i: One of the emirs presented to him horses of the finest breed and beautiful slave-girls, more than the tongue can describe.
sentences.n: فقدم is read as the active فَقَدَّمَ, “presented”, with بعض الأمراء as its subject.

sentences.t: فَأَعْجَبَتْهُ جَارِيَةٌ مِنْهُنَّ فَاسْتَخْلَى بِهَا وَدَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا فِي تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةِ فَعَلِقَتْ مِنْهُ مِنْ سَاعَتِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-aʿjabat-hu jāriyatun minhunna fa-istakhlā bihā wa-dakhala ʿalayhā fī tilka al-laylati fa-ʿaliqat minhu min sāʿatihā
sentences.l: And a slave-girl of them pleased him, and he was alone with her, and went in to her in that night, and she conceived from him from her hour.
sentences.i: One of the girls pleased him, and he took her aside and went in to her that night, and she conceived by him at once.
sentences.n: استخلى بها, “he was alone with her”: بِـ here marks the person he withdrew with. علقت منه, “she conceived by him”, literally “clung from him”.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ مُدَّةٍ رَجَعَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ مِنْ سَفَرِهِ وَأَخْبَرَهُ بِخَبَرِ أَخِيهِ شَرْكَانَ وَأَنَّهُ قَادِمٌ عَلَيْهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ يَنْبَغِي أَنْ تَخْرُجَ وَتُلَاقِيَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda muddatin rajaʿa al-wazīru dandānu min safarihi wa-akhbarahu bi-khabari akhīhi sharrukāna wa-annahu qādimun ʿalayhi wa-qāla lahu yanbaghī an takhruja wa-tulāqiyahu
sentences.l: And after a while the vizier Dandān returned from his journey, and informed him of the news of his brother Sharrukān, and that he was coming upon him, and said to him: It is fitting that you go out and meet him.
sentences.i: After a time the vizier Dandān came back from his journey and told him the news of his brother Sharrukān, that he was on his way to him, and said: “You ought to go out and meet him.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً فَخَرَجَ إِلَيْهِ مَعَ خَوَاصِّ دَوْلَتِهِ مِنْ بَغْدَادَ مَسِيرَةَ يَوْمٍ ثُمَّ نَصَبَ خِيَامَهُ هُنَاكَ لِا نْتِظَارِ أَخِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu ḍawʾu al-makāni samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan fa-kharaja ilayhi maʿa khawāṣṣi dawlatihi min baghdāda masīrata yawmin thumma naṣaba khiyāmahu hunāka li-intiẓāri akhīhi
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to him: Hearing and obedience. And he went out to him with the select of his state from Baghdad a day’s journey, then pitched his tents there for the awaiting of his brother.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān answered: “With hearing and obedience.” He rode out to meet him with the chief men of his court, a day’s journey from Baghdad, and pitched his tents there to wait for his brother.
sentences.n: The print splits لانتظار into لا نتظار; the spacing is kept as printed and read as one word, li-intiẓār, “for the awaiting”.

sentences.t: وَعِنْدَ الصَّبَاحِ أَقْبَلَ الْمَلِكُ شَرْكَانُ فِي عَسَاكِرِ الشَّامِ مَا بَيْنَ فَارِسٍ مِقْدَامٍ وَأَسَدٍ ضِرْغَامٍ وَبَطَلٍ مِصْدَامٍ
sentences.tr: wa-ʿinda al-ṣabāḥi aqbala al-maliku sharrukānu fī ʿasākiri al-shāmi mā bayna fārisin miqdāmin wa-asadin ḍirghāmin wa-baṭalin miṣdāmin
sentences.l: And at the morning King Sharrukān came on in the armies of Syria, between a horseman bold, and a lion fierce, and a hero battering.
sentences.i: At dawn King Sharrukān came up with the armies of Syria — bold horsemen, fierce lions, heroes who batter all before them.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: the three descriptions end in the same pattern, -ām (مقدام، ضرغام، مصدام).

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَشْرَفَتِ الْكَتَائِبُ وَقَدِمَتِ السَّحَائِبُ وَأَقْبَلَتِ الْعَصَائِبُ وَخَفَقَتْ أَعْلَامُ الْمَوَاكِبِ تَوَجَّهَ شَرْكَانُ هُوَ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ لِمُلَاقَاتِهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ashrafati al-katāʾibu wa-qadimati al-saḥāʾibu wa-aqbalati al-ʿaṣāʾibu wa-khafaqat aʿlāmu al-mawākibi tawajjaha sharrukānu huwa wa-man maʿahu li-mulāqātihim
sentences.l: And when the squadrons appeared, and the clouds arrived, and the bands advanced, and the banners of the processions fluttered, Sharrukān set out, he and those with him, to meet them.
sentences.i: When the squadrons came into view, the cloud-like hosts arrived, the companies pressed forward and the banners of the columns fluttered, Sharrukān set out with his men to meet them.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose again, on -āʾib (الكتائب، السحائب، العصائب، المواكب). The “clouds” (سحائب) are the dust-clouds, or the hosts themselves, of the advancing army.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا عَايَنَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ أَخَاهُ أَرَادَأَنْ يَتَرَجَّلَ إِلَيْهِ فَأَقْسَمَ عَلَيْهِ شَرْكَانُ أَنْ لَا يَفْعَلَ ذَلِكَ وَتَرَجَّلَ شَرْكَانُ وَمَشَى خُطُوَاتٍ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ʿāyana ḍawʾu al-makāni akhāhu arāda an yatarajjala ilayhi fa-aqsama ʿalayhi sharrukānu an lā yafʿala dhālika wa-tarajjala sharrukānu wa-mashā khuṭuwātin
sentences.l: And when Ḍawʾ al-Makān sighted his brother, he wanted to dismount to him, but Sharrukān swore to him that he not do that; and Sharrukān dismounted, and walked some steps.
sentences.i: When Ḍawʾ al-Makān saw his brother he wanted to dismount and go to him, but Sharrukān swore that he must not do so; instead Sharrukān dismounted himself and walked a few steps.
sentences.n: The print runs أراد and أن together as ارادان; the spacing is kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا صَارَبَيْنَ يَدَيْ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ رَمَى ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ نَفْسَهُ عَلَيْهِ فَاحْتَضَنَهُ شَرْكَانُ إِلَى صَدْرِهِ وَبَكَيَا بُكَاءًا شَدِيدًا وَعَزَّى بَعْضُهُمَا بَعْضًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ṣāra bayna yaday ḍawʾi al-makāni ramā ḍawʾu al-makāni nafsahu ʿalayhi fa-iḥtaḍanahu sharrukānu ilā ṣadrihi wa-bakayā bukāʾan shadīdan wa-ʿazzā baʿḍuhumā baʿḍan
sentences.l: And when he came to be between the hands of Ḍawʾ al-Makān, Ḍawʾ al-Makān threw himself upon him, and Sharrukān embraced him to his chest, and they both wept a violent weeping, and each consoled the other.
sentences.i: When he stood before Ḍawʾ al-Makān, Ḍawʾ al-Makān threw himself on him and Sharrukān clasped him to his breast, and they wept bitterly and comforted one another.
sentences.n: The print runs صار and بين together (صاربين) and has اى for إلى (“to his chest”), a misprint for الى, corrected here; the spacing is otherwise kept. بكاءا is the edition’s spelling of بكاء.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ رَكِبَ الِاثْنَانِ وَسَارَا وَسَارَ الْعَسْكَرُ مَعَهُمَا إِلَى أَنْ أَشْرَفُوا عَلَى بَغْدَادَ وَنَزَلُوا
sentences.tr: thumma rakiba al-ithnāni wa-sārā wa-sāra al-ʿaskaru maʿahumā ilā an ashrafū ʿalā baghdāda wa-nazalū
sentences.l: Then the two mounted and went, and the army went with them, until they overlooked Baghdad, and they alighted.
sentences.i: Then the two mounted and rode on, with the army behind them, until they came in sight of Baghdad and dismounted.
sentences.n: The print has اى for إلى, a misprint for الى, corrected here.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ طَلَعَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ هُوَ وَأَخُوهُ شَرْكَانُ إِلَى قَصْرِ الْمَلِكِ وَبَاتَا تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ
sentences.tr: thumma ṭalaʿa ḍawʾu al-makāni huwa wa-akhūhu sharrukānu ilā qaṣri al-maliki wa-bātā tilka al-layla
sentences.l: Then Ḍawʾ al-Makān went up, he and his brother Sharrukān, to the palace of the king, and they spent that night.
sentences.i: Then Ḍawʾ al-Makān and his brother Sharrukān went up to the king’s palace and spent the night there.

sentences.t: وَعِنْدَ الصَّبَاحِ خَرَجَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَأَمَرَأَنْ يَجْمَعُوا الْعَسَاكِرَ مِنْ كُلِّ جَانِبٍ وَيُنَادُوا بِالْغَزْوِ وَالْجِهَادِ
sentences.tr: wa-ʿinda al-ṣabāḥi kharaja ḍawʾu al-makāni wa-amara an yajmaʿū al-ʿasākira min kulli jānibin wa-yunādū bi-al-ghazwi wa-al-jihādi
sentences.l: And at the morning Ḍawʾ al-Makān went out, and commanded that they gather the armies from every side, and proclaim the raid and the striving.
sentences.i: At dawn Ḍawʾ al-Makān came out and ordered the armies to be mustered from every quarter and war and holy war to be proclaimed.
sentences.n: أمر ان is printed run together (وامران). يجمعوا and ينادوا again lack the final nūn of the Classical subjunctive. الغزو والجهاد pairs raiding with jihād, the striving or holy war against the unbelievers.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَقَامُوا يَنْتَظِرُونَ مَجِيءَ الْجُيُوشِ مِنْ سَائِرِ الْبُلْدَانِ وَكُلُّ مَنْ حَضَرَ يُكْرِمُونَهُ وَيَعِدُونَهُ بِالْجَمِيلِ إِلَى أَنْ مَضَى عَلَى ذَلِكَ الْحَالِ مُدَّةُ شَهْرٍ كَامِلٍ وَالْقَوْمُ يَأْتُونَ أَفْوَاجًا مُتَتَابِعَةً
sentences.tr: thumma aqāmū yantaẓirūna majīʾa al-juyūshi min sāʾiri al-buldāni wa-kullu man ḥaḍara yukrimūnahu wa-yaʿidūnahu bi-al-jamīli ilā an maḍā ʿalā dhālika al-ḥāli muddatu shahrin kāmilin wa-al-qawmu yaʾtūna afwājan mutatābiʿatan
sentences.l: Then they stayed, awaiting the coming of the armies from all the lands, and everyone who arrived they honoured and promised with the fair, until there passed upon that state the span of a full month, and the people coming in troops following one another.
sentences.i: Then they stayed on, waiting for the armies to come in from all the lands, honouring each man who arrived and promising him a fine reward, until a full month had passed in this way, with the people still coming in band after band.
sentences.n: The print has اى for إلى, a misprint for الى, corrected here. يعدونه بالجميل, “promise him with the fair”: بِـ marks what is promised.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ شَرْكَانُ لِأَخِيهِ يَا أَخِي أَعْلِمْنِي بِقَضِيَّتِكَ فَأَعْلَمَهُ جَمْعَ مَا وَقَعَ لَهُ مِنَ الْأَوَّلِ إِلَى الْآخِرِ وَبِمَا صَنَعَهُ مَعَهُ الْوَقَّادُ مِنَ الْمَعْرُوفِ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla sharrukānu li-akhīhi yā akhī aʿlimnī bi-qaḍiyyatika fa-aʿlamahu jamʿa mā waqaʿa lahu mina al-awwali ilā al-ākhiri wa-bi-mā ṣanaʿahu maʿahu al-waqqādu mina al-maʿrūfi
sentences.l: Then Sharrukān said to his brother: O my brother, let me know your case. And he let him know the whole of what had befallen him from the first to the last, and what the fire-tender had done with him of kindness.
sentences.i: Then Sharrukān said to his brother: “Brother, tell me your story.” And he told him everything that had befallen him from beginning to end, and all the kindness the fire-tender had shown him.
sentences.n: The print has اى for إلى, a misprint for الى, corrected here. جمع ما وقع له is taken as “the whole of what befell him” (جميع ما would be the usual form); it is kept as printed, doubtful.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ شَرْكَانُ أَمَا كَافَأْتَهُ عَلَى مَعْرُوفِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla sharrukānu a-mā kāfaʾtahu ʿalā maʿrūfihi
sentences.l: And Sharrukān said: Have you not repaid him for his kindness?
sentences.i: Sharrukān said: “Have you not repaid him for his kindness?”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ يَا أَخِي مَا كَافَأْتُهُ إِلَى الْآنَ وَلَكِنْ أُكَافِئُهُ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى لَمَّا أَرْجِعُ مِنَ الْغَزْوَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu yā akhī mā kāfaʾtuhu ilā al-āna wa-lākin ukāfiʾuhu in shāʾa allāhu taʿālā lammā arjiʿu mina al-ghazwati
sentences.l: And he said to him: O my brother, I have not repaid him until now, but I will repay him, if God, exalted, wills, when I return from the raid.
sentences.i: He answered: “Brother, I have not repaid him yet, but I will, God willing, when I return from the campaign.”

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَ——————————حِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The closing formula, as in every night; the print breaks the last word with a rule of dashes.
